note_text: Commercial EUV lithography tools have significantly higher throughput than 75 wafers per hour. ASML’s early production models reached 125 wph as of 2017, while current third-generation systems like the NXE:3800E can process approximately 195 to 220 wafers per hour. https://www.asml.com/en/products/euv-lithography-systems/twinscan-nxe3400b https://www.tomshardware.com/tech-industry/manufacturing/asml-delivers-3rd-generation-euv-chipmaking-tool-for-2nm-and-beyond
claim: An EUV lithography tool can process roughly 75 wafers per hour.
context: An EUV tool can do roughly 75 wafers per hour, and the tool is up roughly 90% of the time.

source_verification.reasoning: The note makes claims that (1) commercial EUV throughput far exceeds 75 wph, (2) early production models reached 125 wph as of 2017, and (3) the NXE:3800E processes ~195–220 wph. The ASML source confirms the NXE:3400B's >=125 wph spec, and the Tom's Hardware source confirms the NXE:3800E's 195–220 wph and its third-generation status. The '2017' date is not explicitly stated in the sources but the NXE:3400B is the early production model referenced, and both core throughput claims are supported. All factual throughput claims are covered.

citations.quote: The 300 mm wafer throughput target specification for the NXE:3400B is larger than or equal to 125 wafers per hour under the following conditions: Dose: 20mJ/cm2, die size: 26 x 33 mm, 96 shots.
citations.explanation: Supports the claim that ASML's early production EUV model reached 125 wph. This is the NXE:3400B, which entered production around 2017.

citations.quote: This week, ASML delivered its 3rd Generation extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography tool, the Twinscan NXE:3800E
citations.explanation: Confirms NXE:3800E is a third-generation EUV system.

citations.quote: The new system can process over 195 wafers per hour at a 30 mJ/cm^2 dose and promises a further increase in performance to 220 wph with a throughput upgrade.
citations.explanation: Supports the 195 to 220 wph throughput claim for the NXE:3800E.
